source_text:
Τέκνα οὖν φωτὸς ἀληθείας, φεύγετε τὸν μερισμὸν καὶ τὰς κακοδιδασκαλίας: ὅπου δὲ ὁ ποιμήν ἐστιν, ἐκεῖ ὡς πρόβατα ἀκολουθεῖτε.
πολλοὶ γὰρ λύκοι ἀξιόπιστοι ἡδονῇ κακῇ αἰχμαλωτίζουσιν τοὺς θεοδρόμους: ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ ἑνότητι ὑμῶν οὐχ ἕξουσιν τόπον.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, urging them to avoid division and false teaching by staying united around their shepherd.
pass_a_gloss: Children therefore of light of truth, flee the division and the evil teachings: but where the shepherd is, there as sheep follow. For many wolves, trustworthy-seeming, with evil pleasure take captive the runners-for-God: but in the unity of you they will not have a place.

choices.why: Keeps the double genitive chain literal, preserving the exact source structure rather than smoothing to 'children of the light of truth'
rejected: children of the light of truth

choices.why: Renders the compound literally as adjective + noun, matching the source's negative force without importing the glossary term 'false teaching' (αἵρεσις)
The adjective means 'worthy of trust' but Ignatius uses it ironically of wolves; the hyphenated rendering preserves the literal sense while signaling the irony
The compound means 'those running for God'; the hyphenated rendering keeps the literal compound sense without smoothing to 'God's runners'
Dative of means rendered literally with 'with', preserving the instrumental force of the dative

pass_b_english: So then, children of the light of truth, flee from division and from evil teachings. Where the shepherd is, there follow as sheep.
For many wolves, seemingly trustworthy, take captive the runners for God with evil pleasure; but in your unity they will have no place.

polish.changed: Clarified the shepherd as the bishop, unified the rendering of 'runners for God,' and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.

notes.quote: So you must align yourselves with the mind of the bishop, as you are already doing.
notes.why: Same leadership role called both “bishop” and “shepherd”.
notes.fix: Use a consistent term or note the synonym.

notes.why: The same Greek term (theodromos) is rendered two different ways, making it unclear they are the same concept.
notes.fix: Pick one English rendering and use it consistently.
